title: Naseeruddin Shah Plays JRD Tata. Jim Sarbh Plays the Man Who Built Titan. This Is India's Boardroom Epic.
excerpt: Made in India: A Titan Story drops today on Amazon MX Player — a six-part drama about how one visionary convinced India's greatest industrialist to make a watch that would change a country's wrist.
body:
There is a story that every Indian who grew up in the 1980s and 1990s knows, even if they have never heard it told properly. It is the story of how India got its first world-class watch. Not a Swiss import. Not a Soviet-era HMT that your father stood in line to buy. A watch designed, manufactured, and marketed entirely by Indians, for Indians, at a time when the idea of an Indian consumer brand competing on aesthetics and precision was considered borderline delusional.

Made in India: A Titan Story, which drops today on Amazon MX Player, tells that story through the eyes of the man who made it happen.

## The Cast That Demanded This Script

Naseeruddin Shah as JRD Tata. Jim Sarbh as Xerxes Desai, Titan's founding managing director. That casting alone signals this is not a corporate hagiography but an actor's piece — a drama about persuasion, belief, and the peculiar loneliness of being the only person in the room who can see the future.

Sarbh, speaking to The Hollywood Reporter India, described what drew him to Desai: "Xerxes Desai struck me as someone who was quietly rebellious, someone unafraid to challenge convention and imagine what didn't yet exist. At its core, it's deeply human — about persistence, instinct, and believing in an idea long before anyone else does."

The six-part series, directed by Robbie Grewal, is based on Vinay Kamath's book *Titan: India's Most Successful Consumer Brand*. The ensemble includes Vaibhav Tatwawadi, Namita Dubey, Lakshvir Saran, and Kaveri Seth.

## The Story Behind the Brand

In pre-liberalized India, the idea of a Tata-backed watch company was met with skepticism from within the Tata Group itself. HMT — the state-owned watchmaker — had a monopoly. Import restrictions meant Swiss brands were luxury items available only to the elite. The market was not asking for disruption.

Xerxes Desai saw it differently. A Parsi industrialist with a background in electronics, Desai believed India could build a quartz watch that was both affordable and aspirational. He needed one thing: JRD Tata's blessing and the Tata brand behind the venture. What followed was years of persuasion, technical problem-solving, and a factory in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, that would eventually produce one of India's most recognized brands.

Titan did not just make watches. It made the idea that Indian manufacturing could be beautiful, precise, and globally competitive — a full decade before liberalization made that idea fashionable.

## What the Diaspora Will Recognize

For NRIs, Titan is not just a brand. It is a memory. The gold-toned Titan watch your father wore to the office. The Raga your mother received on an anniversary. The Fastrack your older cousin brought home from college, signaling that they had arrived somewhere worth being.

The series appears to understand this emotional register. Namita Dubey, who plays a key role, described the set dynamic as one where "the characters are making mistakes, they are confused and emotional at the same time — like us." That messiness — the gap between vision and execution, between a boardroom pitch and a factory floor — is where the real drama lives.

Jim Sarbh and Naseeruddin Shah have never worked together on screen before. Sarbh was candid about what it felt like: "I already had a camaraderie with him; I just never got to see it fulfilled earlier on stage or screen. Now I've got that... and I want more."

## Where and How to Watch

Made in India: A Titan Story streams for free on Amazon MX Player starting today, June 3, 2026. No subscription required. The series is available across mobile devices, Fire TV, JioTV, Airtel Xstream, and the Amazon shopping app.

For a diaspora audience that has spent years watching Indian business go from license raj caution to global ambition, this series arrives at exactly the right moment. It is a reminder that before Infosys went to Nasdaq, before Tata Motors bought Jaguar, before Indian founders built billion-dollar startups in Silicon Valley — someone had to convince JRD Tata that India could make a watch.

That someone was Xerxes Desai. And the watch was Titan.
author: Diaspora Desk
